specification.problem: Estimate the mean a=(1/N)sum_x f(x) of a bounded function f:{0,...,N-1}->[0,1] with standard quantum amplitude estimation, with f compiled from an explicit classical table into controlled rotations. This is a standard-background stand-in for the abstract's mean-estimation goal.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny explicit instance (assumed): N=4, n=2 index qubits, 1 ancilla qubit, t phase qubits. Only the amplitude-estimation unitary is built, with no measurement. The paper's novel optimal algorithm, the Aharonov-variant algorithm and the median-finding algorithm are out of scope. No black-box query complexity is certified.

symbols.meaning: bounded function value, given as an explicit classical table
mean of f, the target quantity
integer read from the phase register
state-preparation unitary: Hadamards on the index register followed by U_f

equations.label: Oracle rotation
equations.description: Controlled Y-rotation on the ancilla for each index x, with angles taken from the explicit table.
equations.justification: Proposed standard construction for encoding the mean as an amplitude. The abstract does not specify it.
assumptions: f is given explicitly and compiled into gates

equations.label: State preparation
equations.description: The probability of ancilla=1 equals the mean of f.
equations.justification: Direct computation from eq_1 and the uniform superposition.

equations.label: Grover iterate
equations.latex: Q=-A S_0 A^\dagger S_\chi,\quad S_\chi=I\otimes Z_{anc},\quad S_0=I-2|0\rangle\langle0|,\quad Q\text{ has eigenphases }e^{\pm i2\theta},\ \sin^2\theta=a
equations.description: Amplitude-amplification iterate. Its eigenphases encode the mean a.
assumptions: global sign conventions are fixed as written; S_chi marks the ancilla=1 component

equations.label: Phase estimation circuit
equations.description: Unitary acting on the phase register and the n+1 system qubits, starting from |0>. Controlled-Q^(2^j) is controlled by phase qubit j.
assumptions: the phase register is little-endian, so qubit j has weight 2^j
the inverse QFT matches this convention

equations.label: Decoding and error
equations.description: Classical decoding of the measured y and the standard error bound.
equations.justification: Standard amplitude estimation theorem. It gives O(1/epsilon) applications of A for additive error epsilon.
assumptions: the bound applies to ideal simulation
the paper's own algorithm may use a different method

registers.name: idx
registers.size: n=log2 N (2 in the tiny instance)

specification.initial_state: All qubits in |0>, ordered phase, idx, anc.

steps.description: Apply H on the phase register. Apply H on idx, then U_f (controlled R_y on anc for each x) to build A.
Apply controlled-Q^(2^j) from phase qubit j, for j=0..t-1.
Apply the inverse QFT on the phase register.
Outside the unitary, measure the phase register to get y and compute a_hat.

specification.measurement: Not part of the circuit. Measure the phase register in the computational basis and read y.
specification.classical_postprocessing: a_hat = sin^2(pi*y/2^t). Both y and 2^t-y give the same estimate.
assumptions: Choice of standard amplitude estimation as the construction, and N=4, t=3 as the tiny instance, is mine.
f values are compiled into gates, so the circuit is not black-box and no query complexity is certified.
missing_information: The paper's novel asymptotically optimal algorithm is not specified in the abstract.
The Aharonov-variant algorithm is not specified.
The median algorithm over an arbitrary distance function is not specified.
